name: Jane Schoenbrun
bio: Jane Flannery Schoenbrun (born February 5, 1987) is an American filmmaker, known for directing the films We're All Going to the World's Fair, I Saw the TV Glow, and Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma. Raised in Brooklyn, New York, their works are renowned for pushing the boundaries of the horror genre, dealing with themes of sex and gender, and the relationships of young people to media.

credits.title: I Saw the TV Glow
credits.overview: In late-'90s suburbia, lonely teenager Owen meets Maddy, who introduces him to a mysterious late-night TV show. Questions begin to arise about why the show sometimes seems more real than their own lives, as their view of reality begins to crack.

credits.overview: This feature-length “mixtape” curated by Jane Schoenbrun and Jordan Wippell reintroduces a stunning body of work by Kati Kelli, an outsider YouTube artist who ran “Girl Internet Show” before her passing in 2019.
